title: Scenario runner: the build author turn is capped at 80 turns, so no mid-tier build can finish; expose --author-max-turns / --ask-max-turns with tier-sized defaults
body:
epic:#3600#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPXwX1YfHyKJUh4agu

Filing-gate category: ① defect with a measured reproduction. It follows #30982 (landed, PR #31096). Its new trace made this one visible. Routing, verbatim: 「能交给车队开发的你不要自己开发」. Epic: objectstack-ai/cloud#3600.

## Measured (re-run 2026-11-07, main `2178d80c`, `--author-timeout 60`, scratch)

| Card | Build author turn |
|:--|:--|
| asset_lifecycle | `error_max_turns` · 23m 34s |
| requisition_to_receipt | `error_max_turns` · 15m 05s |
| travel_expense | `error_max_turns` · 14m 48s |

All three are now correctly "not measured", which is #30982 working. But no mid-tier build can finish, because the author turn's turn cap is fixed at 80 (`ClaudeCodeDriver`, `driver.ts:285`, `maxTurnsAuthor ?? 80`; the ask cap is `maxTurnsAsk ?? 12` at `:311`). The CLI exposes neither. The control cards finish in 17–21 turns. A 7–8-object build with permission sets, flows, approvals, views, a dashboard and agent actions needs several times that.

## Ask

1. CLI options `--author-max-turns N` (build and iterate turns) and `--ask-max-turns N` (persona turns), threaded to the driver like `--author-timeout`.
2. Defaults sized by the card's `tier` (#30970), for example `control` 80, `starter` 300 and `delivery` 600. Record the cap used on the run record and on the scorecard's author row.
3. Pin it: a test that the flag reaches the CLI argument list, and one that the tier default applies when the flag is absent.

Verification: the epic seat re-runs the six `starter` cards after this lands.

Reader: the `domain:devx` lane seat, from `pm:queue`. p1, because it blocks every mid-tier measurement.
